binders: The first main conjunct universally quantifies m ∈ ℕ, including m = 0; write V_m = {v : Fin m → ℝ}, the real vector space with coordinates indexed 0,...,m-1.
For each m, it universally quantifies q : ℝ → ℝ → V_m, flux : V_m → V_m, and x,t ∈ ℝ. The first argument of q is position and the second is time.
The first conclusion universally quantifies a,b ∈ ℝ and then quantifies over Lebesgue-almost every τ ∈ ℝ. The variable s in the differentiated function is a bound time variable.
The second conclusion universally quantifies each candidate spatial derivative qx ∈ V_m.
The fourth conclusion universally quantifies fluxDerivative : V_m → L_ℝ(V_m,V_m), where L_ℝ denotes continuous real-linear maps.
Within LocalDef001, qt ∈ V_m and then qx ∈ V_m are existentially quantified for the given q, fluxDerivative, x,t. Both derivative requirements and the equation must hold for the same pair.

The second main conjunct independently asserts existence of q : ℝ → ℝ → V_1, then flux : V_1 → V_1, then x ∈ ℝ, then t ∈ ℝ. These are jointly chosen witnesses; there are no preceding universal parameters governing this existential conjunct.
hypotheses: For the universal implication, q and flux satisfy LocalDef002: for every a,b,r ∈ ℝ, ξ ↦ q(ξ,r) is interval integrable from a to b; for every y,s,r ∈ ℝ, τ ↦ flux(q(y,τ)) is interval integrable from s to r.
The same hypothesis requires, for every a,b,s,r ∈ ℝ, ∫_a^b q(ξ,r) dξ - ∫_a^b q(ξ,s) dξ = ∫_s^r [flux(q(a,τ)) - flux(q(b,τ))] dτ.
The second hypothesis of the universal implication is that ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) is not continuous at x.
The existential main conjunct has no external hypotheses; it requires its witnesses to satisfy LocalDef002, 0 < t, and discontinuity of ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) at x.
conclusions: For every a,b ∈ ℝ, for Lebesgue-almost every τ ∈ ℝ, the vector-valued function s ↦ ∫_a^b q(ξ,s) dξ has derivative flux(q(a,τ)) - flux(q(b,τ)) at s = τ.
For every qx ∈ V_m, the spatial slice ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) does not have derivative qx at x.
The spatial slice ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) is not differentiable over ℝ at x.
For every fluxDerivative : V_m → L_ℝ(V_m,V_m), there do not exist qt,qx ∈ V_m such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt + fluxDerivative(q(x,t))(qx) = 0.

There exist a one-coordinate state function q, a flux function on that one-coordinate state space, and real x,t such that the full global integral balance and slice integrability requirements hold, t > 0, and the spatial slice at t is discontinuous at x.
mathematical_definitions: V_m is the finite product of m copies of ℝ, with coordinatewise arithmetic, the finite product normed vector space structure, and the product topology.
For a vector-valued f and real a,b, ∫_a^b f dξ means the Bochner integral over (a,b] minus the Bochner integral over (b,a], with respect to Lebesgue measure.
Interval integrability requires integrability on both oriented half-open interval sets (a,b] and (b,a]; only one can be nonempty.

Having derivative v at r means an ordinary full-neighborhood, two-sided real-parameter derivative with vector value v; equivalently here, the difference quotient tends to v as the nonzero increment tends to zero.
Differentiability at a point means existence of a continuous real-linear Fréchet derivative there.
LocalDef001 requires both partial derivatives at the specified point and their equation qt + A(q(x,t))(qx) = 0, where A is the supplied operator assignment.
LocalDef002 is the conjunction of spatial slice integrability, fixed-position temporal flux integrability, and the stated integral balance for all real spatial and temporal endpoints.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Two assertions hold together. First, in every finite real coordinate dimension, if q and flux satisfy the global interval integral balance with all the stated slice integrability conditions, and q's spatial slice at time t is discontinuous at x, then every fixed spatial interval has a total state integral whose time derivative equals the flux at its first endpoint minus the flux at its second endpoint for almost every real time. At the specified discontinuity the spatial slice has no derivative vector and is not real differentiable. Moreover, for every assignment A of continuous real-linear operators to states, it is impossible to have both temporal and spatial derivative vectors at (x,t) satisfying qt + A(q(x,t))(qx) = 0. Second, there exists such an integral-balance pair q,flux with one real coordinate and with a spatial discontinuity at some strictly positive time.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The universal dimension includes zero. For m = 0 the state space is a singleton, so every spatial slice is continuous and the discontinuity hypothesis is impossible; that case of the implication is vacuous.
The existential assertion is specifically in dimension one. It does not assert existence in every dimension or for a prescribed flux.

All functions have the full real line as both position and time domains. The universal assertion imposes no positivity condition on its time t; only the existential witness time is required to be positive.
The integral balance is required for all real endpoints, with no a < b or s < t assumption. Equal spatial endpoints make the integral derivative assertion trivially zero equals zero.
The quantifier order is for every a,b, for almost every τ. The null exceptional set may depend on a,b; a single common full-measure set valid for all intervals is not asserted.
The almost-everywhere derivative assertion need not hold at the specified discontinuity time t.
The hypothesis already assumes spatial discontinuity. The universal implication does not itself produce a discontinuity or describe its formation from initial data.
Discontinuity is not specified to be a jump, to possess one-sided limits, or to lie on a moving curve. No speed, trajectory, entropy condition, or initial or boundary data are encoded.

The operator assignment named fluxDerivative has no asserted relationship to flux: it need not be its derivative, and the assignment itself need not be continuous. Only each operator value is continuous and real-linear.

Negation of LocalDef001 denies simultaneous derivative existence and the equation. It does not assert that an equation between existing derivatives has a nonzero residual, nor that the temporal derivative fails to exist.
The statement imposes slice integrability, not an explicit joint measurability or joint regularity hypothesis on q. No independent global continuity or differentiability hypothesis is placed on flux.
The balance uses actual point values of flux(q(a,τ)) and flux(q(b,τ)); no separate trace construction or equivalence-class representative is specified.

The explicit integrability hypotheses ensure the displayed interval integrals are genuine integrals on the relevant intervals; the conclusions are not obtained merely from a default value for a nonintegrable function.
